basis: Basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic jaw keratocysts and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; falx calcification generally causes no neurologic impairment.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining odontogenic keratocysts arise from dental epithelium; their intraosseous location does not exclude their dental origin.

basis: Defined as hepatic porphyria with a heme-synthesis defect and bullous skin injury; anemia and corneal injury occur in 5-29%; tooth pigmentation is non-damaging.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the definition explicitly identifies hepatic porphyria, locating the metabolic disease in the liver; this does not imply common hepatic failure.

basis: Developmental disability defines disease; pyloric stenosis and blepharophimosis each occur in 80-99%; unspecified finger/foot morphology does not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: finger and foot abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but their unspecified morphology does not establish damaging skeletal disease.

basis: Inherited peripheral neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and persistent foot deformities affect most patients (>50%) and represent structural damage beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation causes actual muscle wasting and fixed foot deformities in most patients (>50%); these are integral manifestations, not merely transient weakness.

basis: Skin infiltration by malignant mature T cells defines this lymphoma; collective extranodal spread does not establish any additional organ at >=30%; marrow infiltration is uncommon.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a malignant disorder of T lymphocytes, a blood-cell lineage; uncommon marrow involvement does not negate its haematologic identity.

basis: Developmental and blood-cell abnormalities define disease; limb malformations and nail hypoplasia occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79% but are less specifically characterized than the retained limb and nail defects; omitted at the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: hypoplastic toenails and other nail abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting direct appendage abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly and other limb malformations occur in 30-79%; they are associated structural abnormalities rather than the defining core.

basis: Skin/hair/nail dysplasia and oral cleft/dental defects define disease; intellectual disability and hypogonadism each occur in 30-79%. Defining syndactyly is cutaneous.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadism is reported in 30-79% and represents gonadal endocrine dysfunction, beyond reproductive anatomy alone.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: defining syndactyly is explicitly cutaneous; facial skeletal dysmorphism does not establish additional locomotor dysfunction.

basis: Beta2-microglobulin deposits damage joints and bones; median neuropathy and axonal loss occur in 30-79%. Renal failure is antecedent; gastrointestinal and cardiac injury are <30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acquired beta2-microglobulin retention and amyloid deposition do not independently establish endocrine disease or an intrinsic metabolic disorder.

basis: Wound-produced bacterial toxin blocks neuromuscular and autonomic transmission; ocular, swallowing and respiratory findings reflect neural blockade rather than separate organ injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the pre-existing wound is the site of bacterial toxin production; skin damage caused by botulism is not a defining manifestation.

basis: Developmental delay defines disease; hearing impairment and hypermetropia each 2/2, congenital hypothyroidism 1/2. Hip dysplasia (1/2) omitted at cap; evidence is limited.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: congenital hypothyroidism occurs in 1/2 reported patients (50%); clinically important thyroid dysfunction is retained within the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hip dysplasia and joint abnormalities occur in 1/2 patients (50%), but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of thyroid dysfunction.
